Middle East.headline: UN warns of Gaza hypothermia deaths as winter storms flood displaced tents
Middle East.body: The UN migration agency warned on Tuesday of potential deaths from hypothermia in Gaza and called for more funding and shelter supplies ahead of winter after a baby reportedly died from the cold. Heavy rain has already flooded thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians crammed into encampments after the war between Israel and Hamas reduced much of the Gaza Strip to rubble. Last week, a 9-month-old baby living in a tent died from suspected hypothermia, UN agencies and Gaza authorities said, and respiratory illnesses are rising. Americas.body: How to help victims of deadly Venezuela earthquakes Scores of people were killed and hundreds have been injured. Relief efforts are underway after a pair of powerful earthquakes struck north-central Venezuela on Wednesday evening, killing more than 160 people and injuring almost 1,000 as of Thursday morning. Emergency responders were undertaking "intensive rescue operations" early Thursday, searching for people thought to be under the rubble, Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez said. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he spoke with Rodriguez and that the U.S. is sending search and rescue teams to the country. Africa.headline: Sudan drone strikes killed most civilian dead this year, UN says
Africa.body: Sudan drone strikes killed more than 1,630 of the 2,230 civilians whose deaths the UN human rights office has verified in Sudan’s war between January and the end of October, the office said on Tuesday. The figures show how drones have become the main killer of civilians in the war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), letting both sides strike far beyond the front lines. The office said the true toll was likely to be higher. What did the UN report on Sudan drone strikes find? Asia-Pacific.headline: Afghanistan’s economy grows despite rising food insecurity and water crisis: World Bank
Asia-Pacific.body: Afghanistan’s economy is projected to expand by three percent in 2026, supported largely by a strong agricultural harvest. However, declining household incomes, rising food prices and worsening water shortages continue to threaten livelihoods, according to the World Bank’s latest economic assessment. In its Fall 2026 Afghanistan Development Update, released on November 18, the World Bank said economic output per capita is expected to fall by 3.3 percent for the third consecutive year, as population growth is forecast to reach 6.6 percent. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Six months on, accessing hard-to-reach communities key to halting Ebola outbreak
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Statement attributable to Africa CDC, UNFPA, UNICEF, WFP, WHO. Six months into the Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, significant progress has been made in bringing lifesaving services closer to affected communities, despite immense challenges. However, fuelled by ongoing conflict, displacement and humanitarian needs, the outbreak continues to expand, particularly in affected areas. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Plateau, UNICEF deploy CATI teams to combat cholera outbreak in high-risk communities
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Plateau State Government, with technical support from the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), has deployed Case Area Targeted Intervention (CATI) teams to communities affected by or considered at risk of cholera as part of efforts to contain the outbreak and prevent further transmission. The intervention followed a four-day CATI training for government health and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) personnel, with teams subsequently deployed to communities to apply the skills acquired. The field exercise was demonstrated in Angwan Damisa, Jos North Local Government Area, while other suspected and high-risk areas visited included Filin Sata in Angwan Rukuba.
